title: After You, No, After You
premise: During a low-stakes conversation, one traveler offers to let another answer first, then receives the same courtesy back. The question is forgotten before anyone claims a turn.

title: A Nickname That Did Not Survive Its First Test
premise: Someone coins a family nickname for an ordinary habit, tries it again at another parked stop, and gets no sign that anyone else remembers it. The nickname is retired without a formal vote.

title: The Route Debate Has No Preferred Pronunciation
premise: The travelers briefly disagree over which pronunciation of 'route' sounds right, then keep using their preferred versions as before. The camera gives the vote a close finish without establishing what was being voted on.

title: The Correction That Never Reaches the Noun
premise: A traveler begins correcting a harmless word choice in a familiar story, pauses to think, then lets the other version stand. The story continues with both terms in place.

title: Did That Count as a Greeting?
premise: One traveler asks whether a quiet nod counts as hello in the family's usual greeting ritual; replies differ, and the same nod gets used at the next parked stop. Nobody arrives at a definition.

title: The Preface Takes Longer Than the Question
premise: A traveler offers two caveats and a clarification before asking which of two harmless labels to use. The answer is 'either is fine,' and the preamble remains the longest part of the exchange.

title: What 'We'll See' Meant to Each of Us
premise: One traveler says 'we'll see' meaning maybe. Another hears no, because that's what it meant growing up, and the video is the conversation where they work out which one it's meant all trip.

title: Can I Add One Thought?
premise: Stories in the car keep dying of interruption, so a traveler proposes a rule: ask 'Can I add one thought?' before jumping in. The conversations still wander, but now people get to finish their sentences.

title: The Pun's Second Life Is Better Than Its First
premise: A traveler makes a weak pun about the word 'road.' Hours later someone changes one word and makes it worse, and the worse version becomes the trip's running joke.

title: The $40 Story Has a Handshake
premise: Every retelling of the patio furniture sale before the move comes out a little different. The $40 never changes, but the neighbor's oddly formal handshake keeps growing until it's the main event of the family's last day in the house.
